correctness.rationale: The exact component count follows from factorization of independently restricted partitions and independent world markings. The connected-tuple recurrence is exhaustive. Uniform adjacent Bell-ratio asymptotics imply \(U_{s+1}/U_s<\delta<1\) for \(2\le s<n/2\); reflection gives \(U_{n-t}/U_t=(n-t)p^{n-2t}/t\), controlling the complementary tail exponentially. Thus the arbitrary fixed-order asymptotic remainder is proved. Independent brute-force partition enumerations matched all claimed exact identities through \(n=6\) for two relations and \(n=4\) for three relations; those finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The probability of common knowledge for a specified proposition at a specified world is a motivated modal-model invariant, not merely whether some event is knowable. In random uniform S5 frames the join is usually connected, but a pointed common-knowledge truth event has polynomial size due to rare isolated roots; the full fixed-order expansion isolates each small-component mechanism with rigorous finite-size error. This advances beyond a routine connectivity corollary or table lookup.
